en.title: Minimum Sum of Absolute Differences When Pairing Two Arrays One-to-One
en.description:
Use every element of two equal-length arrays exactly once to form n pairs. The same position in b cannot be matched by different positions in a, and different positions holding the same value still count as separate elements. Minimize the total of the absolute differences within each pair.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains a, and the third line contains b. The main raw constraints explicitly say Unknown; this site adds 1≤n≤100000, −10^9≤a[i],b[i]≤10^9. This range does not pretend to be the source's original bounds.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 4 and 0 respectively. In the second example, pair −5 with −3 and 2 with 4; each pair differs by 2.
hints: Sort both arrays in ascending order, pair them in that order, and add up the absolute differences.
